decisions.reason: The two verbs are a trip and a fall for good (meaning decision); Korean uses two different verbs so the contrast stays.

Paul sets tripping against falling down for good (m2). Vietnamese "vấp ngã" would join the two, so the verbs are kept apart, and "luôn" (for good) says what the second one means, as the English Balanced does.

The conjunction can express purpose or result (m3). Japanese has no single word for both; "ために" would state a purpose, while "ほどに" asks about the outcome, which is what Paul's answer goes on to speak of.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be; but by the of them trespass the salvation to the Gentiles, for the to provoke to jealousy them.

en.L: May it not be! But by their trespass salvation [has come] to the Gentiles, so as to make them jealous.
en.B: Certainly not! Rather, through their wrongdoing salvation has come to the Gentiles, so that Israel would become jealous.
en.R: Of course not! Because they did wrong, salvation has come to people who are not Jews. That was meant to make the people of Israel jealous.

es.L: ¡No sea así! Sino que por su transgresión [vino] la salvación a los gentiles, para provocarlos a celos.
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Al contrario, por medio de su transgresión la salvación ha alcanzado a los gentiles, con el fin de despertar los celos de Israel.
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Como ellos hicieron mal, la salvación ha llegado a los que no son judíos. Eso debía hacer que el pueblo de Israel sintiera celos.

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Bali kwa kosa lao wokovu [umewafikia] watu wa mataifa, ili kuwatia wivu.
sw.B: Hasha! Badala yake, kupitia kosa lao wokovu umewafikia watu wa mataifa, ili kuwafanya Waisraeli waone wivu.
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Kwa sababu walikosea, wokovu umewafikia watu wasio Wayahudi. Jambo hilo lilikusudiwa kuwafanya watu wa Israeli waone wivu.

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Mais par leur faux pas, le salut [est venu] aux nations, pour les rendre jaloux.
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Au contraire, par leur faute, le salut est venu aux non-Juifs, pour qu’Israël devienne jaloux.
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Parce qu’ils ont mal agi, le salut est arrivé à ceux qui ne sont pas juifs. Cela devait rendre le peuple d’Israël jaloux.

ko.L: 결코 그럴 수 없습니다! 오히려 그들의 범죄로 구원이 이방 사람들에게 [이르렀으니], 이는 그들을 시기하게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 절대로 그렇지 않습니다! 오히려 그들의 범죄 때문에 구원이 이방 사람들에게 이르렀고, 그것은 이스라엘이 시기하게 하려는 것이었습니다.
ko.R: 절대 아닙니다! 그들이 잘못했기 때문에, 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 구원이 왔습니다. 그것은 이스라엘 백성이 질투하게 하려는 것이었습니다.

vi.L: Không hề như vậy! Nhưng bởi sự vi phạm của họ, sự cứu rỗi [đã đến] cho các dân ngoại, để khiến họ ganh tị.
vi.B: Chẳng hề như vậy! Trái lại, qua sự vi phạm của họ, các dân ngoại đã được cứu, để Y-sơ-ra-ên phải ganh tị.
vi.R: Không đời nào! Vì họ đã làm sai, những người không phải Do Thái đã được cứu. Điều đó là để làm cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ganh tị.

pt.L: Que não aconteça! Mas, pela transgressão deles, a salvação [veio] às nações, para provocá-los a ciúmes.
pt.B: De forma alguma! Pelo contrário, por causa do erro deles a salvação chegou aos não judeus, para que Israel ficasse com ciúmes.
pt.R: Claro que não! Porque eles erraram, a salvação chegou aos que não são judeus. Isso devia deixar o povo de Israel com ciúmes.

am.L: ከቶ አይሁን! ነገር ግን በበደላቸው መዳን ለአሕዛብ [መጣ]፤ [ይህም] እነርሱን ለማስቀናት [ነው]።
am.B: በፍጹም! ይልቁንም እስራኤል እንዲቀና በበደላቸው ምክንያት መዳን ወደ አሕዛብ መጥቷል።
am.R: በጭራሽ! ስሕተት በመሥራታቸው ምክንያት መዳን አይሁድ ወዳልሆኑ ሕዝቦች መጣ። ይህም የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ ለማስቀናት ነበር።

ru.L: Да не будет! Но их проступком спасение [пришло] к язычникам, чтобы вызвать у них ревность.
ru.B: Ни в коем случае! Напротив, через их проступок спасение пришло к язычникам, чтобы Израиль стал ревновать.
ru.R: Конечно, нет! Из-за того, что они согрешили, спасение пришло к людям из других народов. Это было для того, чтобы народ Израиля стал ревновать.

hi.L: ऐसा कभी न हो! पर उनके अपराध से अन्यजातियों को उद्धार [मिला], कि उन्हें जलन दिलाए।
hi.B: कदापि नहीं! बल्कि उनके अपराध के द्वारा अन्यजातियों तक उद्धार पहुँचा है, ताकि इस्राएल के मन में जलन जागे।
hi.R: बिलकुल नहीं! उन्होंने अपराध किया, और इसी के कारण ग़ैर-यहूदियों तक उद्धार पहुँचा। यह इसलिए हुआ कि इस्राएल के लोगों को जलन हो।

uk.L: Нехай не буде! Але через їхній переступ спасіння [прийшло] до язичників, щоб викликати в них ревнощі.
uk.B: Аж ніяк! Навпаки, через їхній переступ спасіння прийшло до язичників, щоб Ізраїль заревнував.
uk.R: Звичайно, ні! Через те, що вони вчинили зле, порятунок прийшов до неюдеїв. Це мало викликати ревнощі в народу Ізраїлю.

ja.L: 決してそうではありません！むしろ、彼らの過ちによって、救いが異邦人に[来ました]。それは彼らにねたみを起こさせるためです。
ja.B: 決してそうではありません！むしろ、彼らの過ちによって救いが異邦人に及び、イスラエルにねたみを起こさせることになったのです。
ja.R: そんなことはありません！彼らがあやまちを犯したので、救いがユダヤ人でない人々に届きました。それは、イスラエルの人々にねたみを起こさせるためでした。

decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:4, 6:2, 9:14; Galatians 2:17).

decisions.choice: trespass: a false step, a wrong
decisions.reason: The noun means a false step, continuing the picture of stumbling. Here it is Israel's refusal to believe in the Messiah (10:16-21).
Paul has just quoted God's words, "I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation" (10:19). Salvation coming to the Gentiles is meant to stir Israel to want it too.

decisions.choice: by their trespass: their trespass was the occasion for salvation to go out
decisions.reason: When Jews rejected the gospel, the apostles turned to the Gentiles (Acts 13:46, 28:28). Paul does not say Israel's sin saves anyone, but that God used it.
Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.
Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the wrong step.
English "them" could seem to mean the Gentiles; Balanced and Readable name Israel.
Readable says what "Gentiles" means, as in 1:16.

"Transgresión" is the settled word for this noun in Paul (Colossians 2:13) and keeps the picture of a false step. Readable says "hicieron mal", as the English Readable says "did wrong". The same applies in verse 12.

"Kosa" (a fault, a wrong step) is the word used for this noun in Colossians 2:13 and Ephesians, and it keeps the picture of stumbling better than "dhambi" (sin). Readable uses the verb "walikosea". The same applies in verse 12.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); ceux qui ne sont pas juifs (R), as in 9:24 (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "the nations", and Paul uses it for everyone who is not a Jew. Literal keeps "nations". "Les païens", the traditional word, today means people with no faith or with pagan religion, which is not Paul’s point; "Gentils" is not French in this sense. Balanced says "les non-Juifs" and Readable "ceux qui ne sont pas juifs", as the English Readable says "people who are not Jews".

decisions.choice: faux pas (L, and R in 11:12); faute (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a false step, and Literal keeps the picture that follows on from "stumbled" in the question before. "Chute" would blur it with "tomber", the fall that Paul denies. Balanced says "faute", as the English Balanced says "wrongdoing".

decisions.choice: "결코 그럴 수 없습니다!" (L); "절대로 그렇지 않습니다!" (B); "절대 아닙니다!" (R), as settled at 3:4
decisions.reason: The same fixed form for each level as through the letter.

decisions.choice: "범죄" (L, B), as in 5:15-20; "잘못하다" (R); "시기하게 하다" (L, B) / "질투하게 하다" (R), as at 10:19
decisions.reason: The trespass is a false step, a wrong (meaning decision); the same Korean as in chapter 5 at Literal and Balanced. Readable uses the plainer "잘못", which keeps the picture of a misstep better than "죄".
The word is a false step (m2), the word kept as "sự vi phạm" in 4:25 and chapter 5. Here it plays on the stumbling of the question before, which "vi phạm" (a step across the line) keeps.

decisions.choice: as nações (L); os não judeus (B); os que não são judeus (R)
decisions.reason: The terms table: Literal keeps the Greek word "nações", Balanced says "os não judeus" where the English says "Gentiles", and Readable says it as a plain clause, as the English Readable does. "Gentios" is church language many readers do not know.

Paraptoma is a false step, a wrong (meaning decision m2), "проступок" at Literal and Balanced as in 4:25 and 5:15-20; Readable says "согрешили", as it says "грех" there. "Падение" (Synodal) would blur it with "fall" in the question just before, which Paul denies.

The Greek word is a false step, a wrong (meaning decision m2), not the general word for sin, which stays "पाप"; trespass is "अपराध" through Romans (4:25, 5:15-20). "ग़लती" would say a mere mistake. The same word stands in verse 12.
paraptōma is a false step, a wrong (m2); "переступ" keeps the picture of stepping aside, as in Romans 4-5. Kept in 11:12; Readable says "хибний крок", "вчинили зле".

The jealousy meant is Israel wanting for itself the salvation the Gentiles now have (m3). "ねたみを起こさせる" keeps the word of Deuteronomy 32:21 as quoted in 10:19, at every level, so that a reader hears the quotation return; the same words are used in verse 14.

source.text: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: If and the trespass of them riches of world and the loss of them riches of Gentiles, how much more the fullness of them.

en.L: Now if their trespass [means] riches for [the] world, and their loss [means] riches for [the] Gentiles, how much more their fullness!
en.B: Now if their wrongdoing means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches their fullness will bring!
en.R: Their wrong step brought great blessing to the world. Their loss brought great blessing to people who are not Jews. So think how much greater the blessing will be when their full number is brought in!

es.L: Y si su transgresión [es] riqueza para [el] mundo, y su pérdida riqueza para [los] gentiles, ¡cuánto más su plenitud!
es.B: Ahora bien, si su transgresión significa riqueza para el mundo, y su pérdida significa riqueza para los gentiles, ¡cuánta mayor riqueza traerá su plenitud!
es.R: Su paso en falso trajo una gran bendición al mundo. Su pérdida trajo una gran bendición a los que no son judíos. ¡{{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} cuánto mayor será la bendición cuando haya entrado su número completo!

sw.L: Na ikiwa kosa lao [ni] utajiri kwa ulimwengu, na hasara yao utajiri kwa watu wa mataifa, utimilifu wao [utakuwa] zaidi sana kiasi gani!
sw.B: Basi, ikiwa kosa lao limeleta utajiri kwa ulimwengu, na kushindwa kwao kumeleta utajiri kwa watu wa mataifa, utimilifu wao utaleta utajiri mkubwa zaidi kiasi gani!
sw.R: Kosa lao lilileta baraka kubwa kwa ulimwengu. Hasara yao iliwaletea baraka kubwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Basi fikirini jinsi baraka itakavyokuwa kubwa zaidi idadi yao kamili itakapoingia!

fr.L: Or si leur faux pas [est une] richesse pour [le] monde, et leur échec une richesse pour [les] nations, combien plus leur plénitude !
fr.B: Or si leur faute a été une richesse pour le monde, et leur échec une richesse pour les non-Juifs, combien plus grande sera la richesse quand ils seront au complet !
fr.R: Leur faux pas a apporté une grande bénédiction au monde. Leur échec a apporté une grande bénédiction à ceux qui ne sont pas juifs. Alors, pensez combien la bénédiction sera plus grande quand ils seront tous rassemblés !

ko.L: 그런데 그들의 범죄가 세상의 부요함이 되고, 그들의 실패가 이방 사람들의 부요함이 되었다면, 그들의 충만함은 얼마나 더 [그러하겠습니까]!
ko.B: 그들의 범죄가 세상에 부요함을 가져다주고 그들의 실패가 이방 사람들에게 부요함을 가져다주었다면, 그들이 다 채워질 때에는 얼마나 더 큰 부요함을 가져다주겠습니까!
ko.R: 그들의 잘못은 세상에 큰 복을 가져왔습니다. 그들의 실패는 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 큰 복을 가져왔습니다. 그렇다면 그들의 수가 다 채워질 때에는 얼마나 더 큰 복이 오겠습니까!

vi.L: Mà nếu sự vi phạm của họ [là] sự giàu có cho thế gian, và sự thất bại của họ [là] sự giàu có cho các dân ngoại, huống chi sự đầy trọn của họ!
vi.B: Mà nếu sự vi phạm của họ đã đem lại sự giàu có cho thế gian, và sự thất bại của họ đã đem lại sự giàu có cho các dân ngoại, thì sự trọn vẹn của họ sẽ đem lại sự giàu có lớn hơn biết bao!
vi.R: Bước sai của họ đã đem lại phước lớn cho thế gian. Sự thất bại của họ đã đem lại phước lớn cho những người không phải Do Thái. Vậy hãy nghĩ xem phước ấy sẽ còn lớn hơn biết bao khi trọn số dân của họ được đem vào!

pt.L: Ora, se a transgressão deles [significa] riqueza para [o] mundo, e a perda deles, riqueza para [as] nações, quanto mais a plenitude deles!
pt.B: Ora, se o erro deles significa riqueza para o mundo, e a perda deles, riqueza para os não judeus, quanto maior riqueza trará a plenitude deles!
pt.R: O passo errado deles trouxe grande bênção para o mundo. A perda deles trouxe grande bênção para os que não são judeus. Então pensem em como a bênção vai ser muito maior quando o número completo deles for trazido!

am.L: በደላቸው ለዓለም ብልጽግና፣ ኪሳራቸውም ለአሕዛብ ብልጽግና [ከሆነ]፣ ሙላታቸውማ እንዴት አብልጦ [ይሆን]!
am.B: በደላቸው ለዓለም ብልጽግና ከሆነ፣ ኪሳራቸውም ለአሕዛብ ብልጽግና ከሆነ፣ ሙላታቸው ምንኛ የበለጠ ብልጽግና ያመጣ ይሆን!
am.R: ስሕተታቸው ለዓለም ታላቅ በረከት አመጣ። ኪሳራቸውም አይሁድ ላልሆኑ ሕዝቦች ታላቅ በረከት አመጣ። እንግዲያስ ሙሉ ቁጥራቸው ሲገባ በረከቱ ምን ያህል የበለጠ እንደሚሆን አስቡት!

ru.L: Если же их проступок — богатство для мира, и их ущерб — богатство для язычников, то насколько больше их полнота!
ru.B: А если их проступок означает богатство для мира, а их поражение — богатство для язычников, то насколько большее богатство принесёт их полнота!
ru.R: Их грех принёс миру великое благословение. Их потеря принесла великое благословение людям из других народов. Подумайте, насколько больше будет благословение, когда войдёт их полное число!

hi.L: और यदि उनका अपराध जगत के लिए धन और उनकी घटी अन्यजातियों के लिए धन [हुई], तो उनकी परिपूर्णता कितना अधिक!
hi.B: और यदि उनका अपराध संसार के लिए धन बना, और उनकी हार अन्यजातियों के लिए धन बनी, तो उनकी परिपूर्णता कितना अधिक धन लाएगी!
hi.R: उनके अपराध से संसार को बड़ी आशिष मिली। उनकी हार से ग़ैर-यहूदियों को बड़ी आशिष मिली। तो सोचो, जब उनकी पूरी गिनती भीतर आ जाएगी, तब आशिष कितनी बड़ी होगी!

uk.L: А якщо їхній переступ — багатство для світу, а їхня втрата — багатство для язичників, то наскільки більше їхня повнота!
uk.B: А якщо їхній переступ означає багатство для світу, а їхня втрата — багатство для язичників, то наскільки більше багатство принесе їхня повнота!
uk.R: Їхній хибний крок приніс великі благословення світові. Їхня втрата принесла великі благословення неюдеям. Тож подумайте, наскільки більшим буде благословення, коли їх буде приведено в повному числі!

ja.L: さて、もし彼らの過ちが世にとっての富[となり]、彼らの敗北が異邦人にとっての富[となる]のなら、彼らの満ちることは、なおさらどれほど[の富となるでしょう]！
ja.B: 彼らの過ちが世の富となり、彼らの失敗が異邦人の富となるのなら、彼らの数が満ちるときには、どれほど豊かな富がもたらされることでしょう！
ja.R: イスラエルのあやまちは、世界の人々に大きな祝福をもたらしました。彼らの失敗は、ユダヤ人でない人々に大きな祝福をもたらしました。それなら、彼らの数が満ちて、みな迎え入れられるときには、どれほど大きな祝福になるか考えてみてください！

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, the nations beyond Israel
decisions.reason: Parallel to "the Gentiles", the world here is the human race to whom the gospel now goes.

decisions.choice: their loss: their defeat or failure
alternatives: their reduction to a small number, in contrast with their "fullness"
decisions.reason: The noun means a defeat or loss. Set against "fullness", some take it to mean that Israel has been reduced to a remnant.

decisions.choice: their fullness: their full number, Israel restored as a whole
decisions.reason: The same word is used of "the full number of the Gentiles" in verse 25, and verse 26 says that all Israel will be saved. Paul looks forward to the time when Israel as a whole is brought in.

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If Israel's failure has brought such blessing, their restoration will bring far more, as verse 15 says.
Readable says what the picture of riches means: spiritual blessing.

decisions.choice: when their full number is brought in
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning decision and uses the same wording as verse 25.
Readable says what "Gentiles" means.
The English Readable says "think how much greater". Spanish puts the invitation to the readers in a plural verb, so it carries a plural_you span.

decisions.choice: leur plénitude (L); quand ils seront au complet (B); quand ils seront tous rassemblés (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as their full number, Israel restored as a whole. "Plénitude" keeps the Greek word, the same as "the fullness of the Gentiles" in 11:25, but it is abstract; Balanced and Readable say the full number in plain words. "Conversion" would say more than the Greek does.
Their fullness is their full number, Israel restored as a whole (meaning decision, footnoted). Literal keeps the noun; Balanced and Readable say it with a verb.
Riches here are spiritual blessing; Readable says "큰 복", as the English Readable says "great blessing".

The meaning decision reads the word as their full number, Israel restored as a whole, with a footnote. Literal and Balanced keep a word for fullness that leaves the footnoted sense open; Readable says full number, as the English Readable does.
"Huống chi" is the form kept for this argument from the lesser to the greater (m4) since 5:9.
The same Greek word as "the full number" in verse 25 (meaning decision m3); Literal and Balanced keep one word for both, Readable says the full number in both places.

decisions.choice: "彼らの満ちること" (L); "彼らの数が満ちる" (B); "彼らの数が満ちて、みな迎え入れられる" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means their full number, Israel restored as a whole (m3). Literal keeps the bare noun; Balanced and Readable say "数が満ちる", the same wording used for the Gentiles in verse 25, so the reader hears the link.

source.text: Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

records.literal_gloss: To you and I speak the Gentiles.

en.L: But I am speaking to you, the Gentiles.
en.B: Now I am speaking to you who are Gentiles.
en.R: Now I am speaking to you who are not Jews.

es.L: Pero a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hablo, a los gentiles.
es.B: Ahora me dirijo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los gentiles.
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} hablo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que no {{plural_you:son|sois}} judíos.

sw.L: Lakini ninasema nanyi, watu wa mataifa.
sw.B: Sasa ninasema nanyi mlio watu wa mataifa.
sw.R: Sasa ninasema nanyi ambao si Wayahudi.

fr.L: Mais c’est à vous, [gens des] nations, que je parle.
fr.B: Je m’adresse maintenant à vous, les non-Juifs.
fr.R: Maintenant, c’est à vous qui n’êtes pas juifs que je parle.

ko.L: 이제 나는 여러분 이방 사람들에게 말합니다.
ko.B: 이제 나는 이방 사람인 여러분에게 말합니다.
ko.R: 이제 나는 유대인이 아닌 여러분에게 말합니다.

vi.L: Nhưng tôi nói với anh chị em, là các dân ngoại.
vi.B: Bây giờ tôi nói với anh chị em là những người dân ngoại.
vi.R: Bây giờ tôi nói với anh chị em, là những người không phải Do Thái.

pt.L: Mas eu falo a vocês, [que são das] nações.
pt.B: Agora falo a vocês, os não judeus.
pt.R: Agora estou falando a vocês, que não são judeus.

am.L: ለእናንተ ለአሕዛብ ግን እናገራለሁ።
am.B: እንግዲህ የምናገረው አሕዛብ ለሆናችሁ ለእናንተ ነው።
am.R: አሁን የምናገረው አይሁድ ላልሆናችሁ ለእናንተ ነው።

ru.L: А вам говорю, язычникам.
ru.B: Теперь я обращаюсь к вам, язычникам.
ru.R: Теперь я говорю вам, людям из других народов.

hi.L: पर मैं तुमसे, अन्यजातियों से, कहता हूँ।
hi.B: अब मैं तुमसे बात कर रहा हूँ जो अन्यजाति हो।
hi.R: अब मैं तुमसे बात कर रहा हूँ जो ग़ैर-यहूदी हो।

uk.L: А вам кажу, язичникам.
uk.B: А тепер я звертаюся до вас, язичників.
uk.R: А тепер я звертаюся до вас, неюдеїв.

ja.L: しかし、わたしは異邦人であるあなたがたに言います。
ja.B: さて、異邦人であるあなたがたに言います。
ja.R: さて、ユダヤ人でないみなさんに言います。

decisions.reason: Paul turns to the Gentile believers among his readers. The church in Rome had both Jewish and Gentile members (1:13, 16:3-15), and here he warns the Gentiles against looking down on Israel.
Readable says what "Gentiles" means.

decisions.choice: язычники (L, B); люди из других народов (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Romans term for the Gentiles, noted where it first addresses the readers in this chapter.

source.text: ἐφ’ ὅσον μὲν οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω, εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Inasmuch as indeed then am I of Gentiles apostle, the ministry of me I glorify, \v 14 if somehow I may provoke to jealousy of me the flesh and may save some of them.

en.L: Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of [the] Gentiles, I glorify my ministry, \v 14 if somehow I may make my flesh jealous and save some of them.
en.B: So since I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I make much of my ministry, \v 14 in the hope that somehow I may make my own flesh and blood jealous and save some of them.
en.R: God sent me as an apostle to people who are not Jews, so I make much of this work. \v 14 I hope that in some way I can make my own people, the Jews, jealous, and save some of them.

es.L: Por cuanto, pues, yo soy apóstol de [los] gentiles, glorifico mi ministerio, \v 14 por si de algún modo provoco a celos a mi carne y salvo a algunos de ellos.
es.B: Así que, ya que soy apóstol para los gentiles, doy gran valor a mi ministerio, \v 14 con la esperanza de despertar de algún modo los celos de los de mi propia sangre y salvar a algunos de ellos.
es.R: Dios me envió como apóstol a los que no son judíos, por eso doy mucha importancia a este trabajo. \v 14 Espero que de alguna manera pueda hacer que mi propio pueblo, los judíos, sienta celos, y así salvar a algunos de ellos.

sw.L: Basi kwa kadiri nilivyo mtume wa watu wa mataifa, naitukuza huduma yangu, \v 14 ili kwa njia yoyote niutie wivu mwili wangu na kuwaokoa baadhi yao.
sw.B: Basi, kwa kuwa mimi ni mtume kwa watu wa mataifa, naipa huduma yangu uzito mkubwa, \v 14 nikitumaini kwamba kwa namna fulani nitawatia wivu ndugu zangu wa damu na kuwaokoa baadhi yao.
sw.R: Mungu alinituma kama mtume kwa watu wasio Wayahudi, kwa hiyo naiona kazi hii kuwa ya maana sana. \v 14 Natumaini kwamba kwa namna fulani nitawafanya watu wa taifa langu, Wayahudi, waone wivu, nami niwaokoe baadhi yao.

fr.L: Dans la mesure donc où moi, je suis apôtre des nations, je glorifie mon ministère, \v 14 si par quelque moyen je peux rendre jalouse ma chair et en sauver quelques-uns.
fr.B: Puisque je suis l’apôtre des non-Juifs, je fais grand cas de mon ministère, \v 14 dans l’espoir de rendre jaloux ceux de mon propre sang et d’en sauver quelques-uns.
fr.R: Dieu m’a envoyé comme apôtre auprès de ceux qui ne sont pas juifs, alors j’accorde une grande importance à ce travail. \v 14 J’espère ainsi rendre jaloux les gens de mon peuple, les Juifs, et en sauver quelques-uns.

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 이방 사람들의 사도인 만큼, 나는 내 직분을 영광스럽게 여깁니다. \v 14 어떻게든 내 육신을 시기하게 하여 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 내가 이방 사람들을 위한 사도인 만큼, 나는 내 직분을 귀하게 여깁니다. \v 14 그렇게 해서 어떻게든 내 동족이 시기하게 하여, 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하고 싶습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 나를 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 사도로 보내셨습니다. 그래서 나는 이 일을 아주 소중하게 여깁니다. \v 14 나는 어떻게든 내 민족인 유대인들이 질투하게 해서, 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하고 싶습니다.

vi.L: Vậy, vì tôi là sứ đồ của các dân ngoại, tôi tôn vinh chức vụ của tôi, \v 14 [mong rằng] bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể khiến [những người cùng] xác thịt với tôi ganh tị và cứu được một số người trong họ.
vi.B: Vì tôi là sứ đồ cho các dân ngoại, tôi rất coi trọng chức vụ của mình, \v 14 mong rằng bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể làm cho đồng bào ruột thịt của tôi ganh tị và cứu được một số người trong họ.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã sai tôi làm sứ đồ cho những người không phải Do Thái, nên tôi rất coi trọng công việc này. \v 14 Tôi mong rằng bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể làm cho chính dân tộc tôi, là người Do Thái, ganh tị, và cứu được một số người trong họ.

pt.L: Enquanto, pois, eu sou apóstolo das nações, glorifico o meu ministério, \v 14 se de algum modo eu provocar a ciúmes a minha carne e salvar alguns deles.
pt.B: Por isso, sendo eu apóstolo dos não judeus, dou grande valor ao meu ministério, \v 14 na esperança de provocar de algum modo ciúmes nos do meu próprio sangue e salvar alguns deles.
pt.R: Deus me enviou como apóstolo aos que não são judeus, por isso dou grande valor a esse trabalho. \v 14 Espero conseguir de algum modo deixar com ciúmes o meu próprio povo, os judeus, e salvar alguns deles.

am.L: እንግዲህ እኔ የአሕዛብ ሐዋርያ እስከ ሆንኩ ድረስ አገልግሎቴን አከብራለሁ፤ \v 14 ምናልባት ሥጋዬን አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን አድን እንደ ሆነ።
am.B: ስለዚህ እኔ ለአሕዛብ ሐዋርያ እንደ መሆኔ መጠን አገልግሎቴን ከፍ አድርጌ እመለከተዋለሁ፤ \v 14 ይህንም የማደርገው በሆነ መንገድ የሥጋ ዘመዶቼን አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን አድን ይሆናል ብዬ ተስፋ በማድረግ ነው።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር አይሁድ ወዳልሆኑ ሕዝቦች ሐዋርያ አድርጎ ልኮኛል፤ ስለዚህ ለዚህ ሥራዬ ትልቅ ዋጋ እሰጣለሁ። \v 14 በሆነ መንገድ የገዛ ሕዝቤን፣ አይሁድን፣ አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን ለማዳን ተስፋ አደርጋለሁ።

ru.L: Поскольку я апостол язычников, я прославляю моё служение, \v 14 не вызову ли как-нибудь ревность у моей плоти и не спасу ли некоторых из них.
ru.B: И раз я апостол язычников, я высоко ценю своё служение, \v 14 надеясь, что как-нибудь вызову ревность у своих родных по крови и спасу некоторых из них.
ru.R: Бог послал меня апостолом к людям из других народов, и я очень дорожу этой работой. \v 14 Я надеюсь, что так смогу вызвать ревность у моего народа, у иудеев, и спасти некоторых из них.

hi.L: इसलिए जहाँ तक मैं अन्यजातियों का प्रेरित हूँ, मैं अपनी सेवा की महिमा करता हूँ, \v 14 कि किसी रीति से मैं अपने शरीर में जलन उपजाऊँ और उनमें से कुछ का उद्धार करूँ।
hi.B: इसलिए क्योंकि मैं अन्यजातियों के लिए प्रेरित हूँ, मैं अपनी सेवा को बड़ा महत्त्व देता हूँ, \v 14 इस आशा से कि किसी तरह मैं अपने शरीर के नातेदारों में जलन जगाऊँ और उनमें से कुछ का उद्धार करूँ।
hi.R: परमेश्वर ने मुझे ग़ैर-यहूदियों के पास प्रेरित बनाकर भेजा है, इसलिए मैं इस काम को बहुत महत्त्व देता हूँ। \v 14 मैं आशा करता हूँ कि किसी तरह मैं अपने लोगों, यानी यहूदियों, में जलन जगा सकूँ और उनमें से कुछ का उद्धार करूँ।

uk.L: Оскільки ж я апостол язичників, я прославляю своє служіння, \v 14 чи не викличу якось ревнощів у своїх [родичів] за тілом і не спасу декого з них.
uk.B: Тож оскільки я апостол для язичників, я надаю великої ваги своєму служінню, \v 14 сподіваючись якось викликати ревнощі у своїх кровних родичів і спасти декого з них.
uk.R: Бог послав мене як апостола до неюдеїв, тож я дуже ціную цю працю. \v 14 Я сподіваюся, що якось зможу викликати ревнощі у свого народу, юдеїв, і врятувати декого з них.

ja.L: それで、わたしは異邦人の使徒である限り、自分の務めを栄光あるものとしています。\v 14 もしかしたら、わたしと肉を同じくする者たちにねたみを起こさせ、彼らのうちの何人かを救えるかもしれないと[思うからです]。
ja.B: それで、異邦人のための使徒として、わたしは自分の務めを重んじています。\v 14 なんとかして肉親である同胞にねたみを起こさせ、彼らのうちの何人かでも救いたいと願っているのです。
ja.R: 神はわたしを、ユダヤ人でない人々のための使徒として遣わされました。だからわたしは、この働きを大切にしています。\v 14 そうすれば、同じ民族のユダヤ人にねたみを起こさせ、その中の何人かでも救うことができるかもしれないと願っているのです。

decisions.choice: I glorify: I honor my ministry and make the most of it
alternatives: I praise God for my ministry
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to give glory, but with "my ministry" as its object it means to hold it in honor and give it full weight, in the hope of the result verse 14 names.

decisions.choice: my flesh: my own people, my fellow Jews
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means physical kinship, as in 9:3, "my kindred according to the flesh".

decisions.choice: save some: bring some to salvation through the gospel
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of saving people as the one who brings them the gospel, as in 1 Corinthians 9:22. Elsewhere it is God who saves (11:26).
"Glorify my ministry" sounds odd in English; Balanced and Readable give the sense described in the meaning decision.
Balanced keeps the word "flesh" in a natural English phrase for kin.
Readable says plainly who are meant.

decisions.choice: God sent me as an apostle to people who are not Jews
alternatives: I am an apostle of the Gentiles
decisions.reason: An apostle is one sent; Readable names God as the sender (1:1, 1:5).

Where the English Balanced keeps "flesh" in "my own flesh and blood", Spanish speaks of relatives as those of one's blood; "mi carne y sangre" is not a usual Spanish way of naming one's people. The sense is the kinship the meaning decision describes.
"Mwili wangu" (my body) cannot mean one's relatives in Swahili, so Balanced says "ndugu zangu wa damu" (my blood relatives), the kinship the meaning decision describes. Literal keeps "mwili".
Paul honors his ministry and makes the most of it (meaning decision). "영광을 돌리다" is kept for glorifying God (1:21).
My flesh means my own people, my fellow Jews (meaning decision). Literal keeps the letter's word "육신"; Balanced uses "동족" as at 9:3.
Paul honors his ministry and makes the most of it (m1). Literal keeps "tôn vinh", the verb set for glorify; Balanced and Readable say "coi trọng", as the English says "make much of".

decisions.choice: "[những người cùng] xác thịt với tôi" (L); "đồng bào ruột thịt của tôi" (B)
decisions.reason: My flesh is my own people, my fellow Jews (m2). Literal keeps "xác thịt", the word for flesh through the letter, and brackets what it means; Balanced uses "đồng bào ruột thịt" of 9:3.

Portuguese speaks of kin as "sangue" ("os do meu sangue"); "a minha carne" alone would be read as Paul's body. This keeps a picture word, as the English Balanced "flesh and blood" does; Literal keeps "a minha carne".

decisions.choice: ሥጋዬ (my flesh, L); የሥጋ ዘመዶቼ (my kin, B); የገዛ ሕዝቤ, አይሁድ (my own people, the Jews, R)
decisions.reason: Here flesh means Paul's fellow Jews (meaning note m2), not the sinful nature. Literal keeps the word; Balanced uses the common Amharic phrase for blood relatives; Readable names them.
Literal keeps "плоть", the settled word for sarx, though here it means Paul's own people (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "अपने शरीर" (L); "अपने शरीर के नातेदारों" (B); "अपने लोगों, यानी यहूदियों" (R)
decisions.reason: My flesh means my own people (meaning decision m2). Balanced keeps the key word "शरीर" in an ordinary Hindi phrase for blood relations, as the English keeps "flesh and blood"; Readable names them.
"My flesh" means Paul's own people (m2); a bare "моє тіло" would read as his body, so Literal supplies "родичів" and keeps "за тілом" as in 9:3.

decisions.choice: "わたしと肉を同じくする者たち" (L); "肉親である同胞" (B); "同じ民族のユダヤ人" (R)
decisions.reason: "My flesh" means Paul's fellow Jews, his kin (m2). A bare "わたしの肉" would be unclear in Japanese, so Literal keeps the word 肉 in a phrase for kinship; Balanced uses 肉親, the ordinary word for blood relatives, which also keeps 肉; Readable names the people.

decisions.choice: "栄光あるものとしています" (L); "重んじています" (B)
decisions.reason: With "my ministry" as its object the verb means holding it in honor (m1). "あがめる" is used for worshiping God and would be wrong here; Literal keeps the word 栄光, and Balanced and Readable give the sense.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;

records.literal_gloss: If for the rejection of them reconciliation of world, what the acceptance if not life from dead?

en.L: For if their rejection [means the] reconciliation of [the] world, what [will their] acceptance [be] but life from [the] dead?
en.B: For if their rejection means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean? Nothing less than life from the dead!
en.R: When God set them aside, the world was brought back to God and made friends with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So what will it be like when God takes them back? It will be life from the dead!

es.L: Porque si su rechazo [es la] reconciliación del mundo, ¿qué [será su] aceptación sino vida de entre [los] muertos?
es.B: Porque si su rechazo significa la reconciliación del mundo, ¿qué significará su aceptación? ¡Nada menos que vida de entre los muertos!
es.R: Cuando Dios los apartó, el mundo pudo volver a Dios y ser {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amigo. Entonces, ¿cómo será cuando Dios los reciba de nuevo? ¡Será vida de entre los muertos!

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa kukataliwa kwao [ni] upatanisho wa ulimwengu, kupokelewa kwao [kutakuwa] nini, isipokuwa uzima kutoka kwa wafu?
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa kukataliwa kwao kunaleta upatanisho wa ulimwengu, kupokelewa kwao kutaleta nini? Si kitu kingine ila uzima kutoka kwa wafu!
sw.R: Mungu alipowaweka kando, ulimwengu ulirudishwa kwa Mungu na kuwa rafiki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Basi itakuwaje Mungu atakapowapokea tena? Itakuwa uzima kutoka kwa wafu!

fr.L: Car si leur rejet [est la] réconciliation du monde, que [sera leur] accueil, sinon une vie d’entre [les] morts ?
fr.B: Car si leur rejet a été la réconciliation du monde, que sera leur accueil ? Rien de moins que la vie d’entre les morts !
fr.R: Quand Dieu les a mis de côté, le monde a été ramené à Dieu et a fait la paix avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors, que se passera-t-il quand Dieu les reprendra ? Ce sera la vie qui sort de la mort !

ko.L: 그들을 버리심이 세상의 화해가 된다면, 그들을 받아들이심은 죽은 사람들 가운데서 [나는] 생명이 아니면 무엇이겠습니까?
ko.B: 하나님께서 그들을 버리신 것이 세상과 하나님의 화해를 가져왔다면, 그들을 받아들이시는 것은 무엇을 가져오겠습니까? 그것은 바로 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나는 생명입니다!
ko.R: 하나님께서 그들을 한쪽으로 제쳐 두셨을 때, 세상 사람들이 하나님께 돌아와 하나님의 친구가 되었습니다. 그렇다면 하나님께서 그들을 다시 받아들이실 때에는 어떻겠습니까? 그것은 죽은 사람들이 다시 살아나는 것과 같은 일일 것입니다!

vi.L: Vì nếu việc họ bị loại bỏ [là] sự hòa giải cho thế gian, thì việc [họ được] tiếp nhận [sẽ là] gì, nếu không phải là sự sống từ kẻ chết?
vi.B: Vì nếu việc họ bị gạt sang một bên đã đem thế gian đến chỗ được hòa giải, thì việc họ được tiếp nhận sẽ là gì? Không gì khác hơn là sự sống từ cõi chết!
vi.R: Khi Đức Chúa Trời gạt họ sang một bên, thế gian được đem trở về với Đức Chúa Trời và trở nên bạn hữu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vậy khi Đức Chúa Trời nhận họ trở lại thì sẽ ra sao? Đó sẽ là sự sống từ cõi chết!

pt.L: Pois, se a rejeição deles [significa a] reconciliação do mundo, que [será a] aceitação [deles], senão vida dentre [os] mortos?
pt.B: Pois, se a rejeição deles significa a reconciliação do mundo, o que significará a aceitação deles? Nada menos que vida dentre os mortos!
pt.R: Quando Deus os deixou de lado, o mundo voltou para Deus e fez as pazes com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Então, como vai ser quando Deus os receber de volta? Vai ser vida dentre os mortos!

am.L: መጣላቸው የዓለም መታረቅ ከሆነ፣ መቀበላቸውማ ከሙታን [የሚገኝ] ሕይወት እንጂ ሌላ ምን [ይሆናል]?
am.B: መጣላቸው የዓለምን መታረቅ ካመጣ፣ መቀበላቸው ምን ማለት ይሆን? ከሙታን መነሣትን ያህል ሕይወት ነው!
am.R: እግዚአብሔር እነርሱን ወደ ጎን ባደረጋቸው ጊዜ ዓለም ወደ እግዚአብሔር ተመልሶ ከእርሱ ጋር ታረቀ። ታዲያ እግዚአብሔር መልሶ ሲቀበላቸው ምን ይሆን? ከሞት እንደ መነሣት ያለ ሕይወት ይሆናል!

ru.L: Ведь если их отвержение — примирение мира, то что [будет] принятие, как не жизнь из мёртвых?
ru.B: Ведь если их отвержение означает примирение мира, то что будет означать их принятие? Не что иное, как жизнь из мёртвых!
ru.R: Когда Бог отстранил их, мир вернулся к Богу и примирился с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. Что же будет, когда Бог снова примет их? Это будет жизнь из мёртвых!

hi.L: क्योंकि यदि उनका ठुकराया जाना जगत का मेल [हुआ], तो उनका ग्रहण किया जाना मरे हुओं में से जीवन के सिवा क्या होगा?
hi.B: क्योंकि यदि उनके ठुकराए जाने का अर्थ संसार का परमेश्वर से मेल है, तो उनके ग्रहण किए जाने का अर्थ क्या होगा? मरे हुओं में से जीवन से कम कुछ नहीं!
hi.R: जब परमेश्वर ने उन्हें अलग कर दिया, तब संसार का परमेश्वर से मेल कराया गया और वह परमेश्वर का मित्र बन गया। तो जब परमेश्वर उन्हें वापस ले लेंगे, तब कैसा होगा? वह तो मरे हुओं में से जी उठने जैसा होगा!

uk.L: Бо якщо їхнє відкинення — примирення світу, то що [буде їхнє] прийняття, як не життя з мертвих?
uk.B: Бо якщо їхнє відкинення означає примирення світу, то що означатиме їхнє прийняття? Ніщо інше, як життя з мертвих!
uk.R: Коли Бог відсунув їх убік, світ повернувся до Бога і примирився з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}. То що ж буде, коли Бог прийме їх назад? Це буде життя з мертвих!

ja.L: もし彼らが捨て置かれることが世の和解[である]なら、彼らが受け入れられることは、死者の中からの命でなくて何でしょうか？
ja.B: もし彼らが捨て置かれたことが世の和解となったのなら、彼らが受け入れられることは何を意味するでしょうか？それはまさに、死者の中からの命です！
ja.R: 神が彼らをわきに置かれたとき、世界の人々は神のもとに連れ戻され、神と仲直りしました。それなら、神が彼らをもう一度受け入れられるときは、どうなるでしょうか？それは、死んだ人たちの中からよみがえる命です！

decisions.choice: their rejection: God's setting them aside
decisions.reason: The phrase could mean that Israel rejected or that Israel was rejected. The matching phrase "their acceptance" most naturally means God accepting them, so "their rejection" is God's setting them aside for a time. This does not contradict verses 1-2: it is not a final casting off.

decisions.choice: the reconciliation of the world: people of all nations brought back into peace with God
decisions.reason: Reconciliation means ending hostility and restoring friendship (5:10-11; 2 Corinthians 5:18-20). "The world" is humanity beyond Israel.

decisions.choice: life from the dead: something as great as resurrection
alternatives: the resurrection of the dead at the end of the age
a picture of new spiritual life for the world
decisions.reason: Paul may mean that Israel's acceptance will come with the final resurrection, or he may be using resurrection as a picture of an overwhelming blessing. The words allow both, and the translation keeps them as they are.

decisions.choice: what will their acceptance mean? Nothing less than life from the dead!
alternatives: what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the question "what ... if not" into a question and an answer.

decisions.choice: When God set them aside, the world was brought back to God and made friends with him
alternatives: their rejection is the reconciliation of the world
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains, and says what reconciliation is.

Swahili must choose between "their rejecting" and "their being rejected", which the Greek noun leaves open. Following the meaning decision, both nouns are passive: God sets them aside and God accepts them.

decisions.choice: "버리심", "받아들이심" with the honorific (L); "하나님께서 ... 버리신 것" (B); "한쪽으로 제쳐 두셨을 때" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "their rejection" as God's setting them aside, and footnotes the other reading. The honorific nouns make God the one who acts even at Literal.
The letter's word for reconciliation at each level.

decisions.choice: "bị loại bỏ" (L); "bị gạt sang một bên" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads this as God setting them aside, with a footnote for their own rejection of the gospel. "Ruồng bỏ" is kept for the verb of 11:1-2, which Paul has just denied, so a different word is used; Balanced and Readable say "set aside", as the English Readable does.
The noun is God's taking them back, the counterpart of his setting them aside (መጣላቸው); Readable makes God the subject.
The settled Romans term for reconciliation (5:10-11), kept at every level.
The Romans key term for reconciliation, "मेल कराना"; Balanced and Readable say with whom: with God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "捨て置かれる" (L, B); "わきに置かれた" (R)
decisions.reason: This is God's setting Israel aside for a time, not the final casting off denied in verses 1-2 (m1). "退ける" is kept for the verb of verses 1-2, and "捨てられる" would sound final; "捨て置く" and "わきに置く" say that they have been left aside.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀπαρχὴ ἁγία, καὶ τὸ φύραμα· καὶ εἰ ἡ ῥίζα ἁγία, καὶ οἱ κλάδοι.

records.literal_gloss: If and the firstfruit holy, also the lump; and if the root holy, also the branches.

en.L: Now if the firstfruit [is] holy, so [is] the lump; and if the root [is] holy, so [are] the branches.
en.B: If the portion of dough offered as firstfruits is holy, so is the whole batch; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
en.R: If the first piece of dough is offered to God and is holy, the whole batch of dough is holy too. And if the root of a tree is holy, so are its branches.

es.L: Y si las primicias [son] santas, también la masa; y si la raíz [es] santa, también las ramas.
es.B: Si la porción de masa ofrecida como primicias es santa, también lo es toda la masa; y si la raíz es santa, las ramas lo son también.
es.R: Si el primer pedazo de la masa se ofrece a Dios y es santo, toda la masa también es santa. Y si la raíz de un árbol es santa, también lo son sus ramas.

sw.L: Na ikiwa limbuko [ni] takatifu, donge pia; na ikiwa mzizi [ni] mtakatifu, matawi pia.
sw.B: Ikiwa sehemu ya unga uliokandwa inayotolewa kama limbuko ni takatifu, basi donge zima ni takatifu; na ikiwa mzizi ni mtakatifu, matawi nayo ni matakatifu.
sw.R: Kipande cha kwanza cha unga kikitolewa kwa Mungu na kuwa kitakatifu, unga wote uliobaki ni mtakatifu pia. Na mzizi wa mti ukiwa mtakatifu, matawi yake nayo ni matakatifu.

fr.L: Or si les prémices [sont] saintes, la pâte aussi [l’est] ; et si la racine [est] sainte, les branches aussi [le sont].
fr.B: Si la part de pâte offerte comme prémices est sainte, toute la pâte l’est aussi ; et si la racine est sainte, les branches le sont aussi.
fr.R: Si le premier morceau de pâte est offert à Dieu et qu’il est saint, toute la pâte est sainte aussi. Et si la racine d’un arbre est sainte, ses branches le sont aussi.

ko.L: 첫 [반죽]이 거룩하면 [온] 덩이도 그러하고, 뿌리가 거룩하면 가지들도 그러합니다.
ko.B: 처음 바친 반죽이 거룩하면 반죽 전체도 거룩하고, 뿌리가 거룩하면 가지들도 거룩합니다.
ko.R: 반죽의 첫 덩이를 하나님께 바쳐서 그것이 거룩하면, 반죽 전체도 거룩합니다. 또 나무의 뿌리가 거룩하면, 그 가지들도 거룩합니다.

vi.L: Mà nếu phần đầu mùa [là] thánh, thì cả khối bột [cũng vậy]; và nếu rễ [là] thánh, thì các nhánh [cũng vậy].
vi.B: Nếu phần bột đầu tiên được dâng làm của đầu mùa là thánh, thì cả mẻ bột cũng thánh; và nếu rễ là thánh, thì các nhánh cũng thánh.
vi.R: Nếu miếng bột đầu tiên được dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời và là thánh, thì cả mẻ bột cũng thánh. Và nếu rễ cây là thánh, thì các nhánh của nó cũng thánh.

pt.L: Ora, se as primícias [são] santas, também a massa; e, se a raiz [é] santa, também os ramos.
pt.B: Se a porção de massa oferecida como primícias é santa, toda a massa também é; e, se a raiz é santa, os ramos também são.
pt.R: Se o primeiro pedaço da massa é oferecido a Deus e é santo, toda a massa também é santa. E, se a raiz de uma árvore é santa, os galhos também são.

am.L: በኩራቱ ቅዱስ ከሆነ ሊጡም [ቅዱስ ነው]፤ ሥሩም ቅዱስ ከሆነ ቅርንጫፎቹም [ቅዱሳን ናቸው]።
am.B: በኩራት ሆኖ የቀረበው የሊጥ ቁራሽ ቅዱስ ከሆነ ሊጡ ሁሉ ቅዱስ ነው፤ ሥሩም ቅዱስ ከሆነ ቅርንጫፎቹም ቅዱሳን ናቸው።
am.R: የሊጡ የመጀመሪያው ቁራሽ ለእግዚአብሔር ተሰጥቶ ቅዱስ ከሆነ፣ ሊጡ ሁሉ ደግሞ ቅዱስ ነው። የዛፍም ሥር ቅዱስ ከሆነ ቅርንጫፎቹም እንዲሁ ቅዱሳን ናቸው።

ru.L: Если же начаток свят, то и тесто; и если корень свят, то и ветви.
ru.B: Если часть теста, принесённая как первый дар Богу, свята, то свято и всё тесто; и если корень свят, то святы и ветви.
ru.R: Если первый кусок теста приносят Богу и он свят, то и всё тесто тоже свято. И если корень дерева свят, то святы и его ветви.

hi.L: और यदि पहला फल पवित्र है, तो गूँधा हुआ आटा भी; और यदि जड़ पवित्र है, तो डालियाँ भी।
hi.B: यदि पहले फल के रूप में चढ़ाया गया आटे का भाग पवित्र है, तो पूरा गूँधा हुआ आटा भी पवित्र है; और यदि जड़ पवित्र है, तो डालियाँ भी पवित्र हैं।
hi.R: अगर गूँधे हुए आटे का पहला हिस्सा परमेश्वर को चढ़ाया जाए और वह पवित्र हो, तो सारा आटा भी पवित्र होता है। और अगर पेड़ की जड़ पवित्र है, तो उसकी डालियाँ भी पवित्र हैं।

uk.L: А якщо першоплід святий, то й заміс; і якщо корінь святий, то й гілки.
uk.B: Якщо частка тіста, принесена як першоплоди, свята, то святий і весь заміс; і якщо корінь святий, то святі й гілки.
uk.R: Якщо перший шматок тіста принесено Богові і він святий, то й усе тісто святе. І якщо корінь дерева святий, то святі і його гілки.

ja.L: さて、初穂が聖なるものであれば、こね粉の全体もそうです。また、根が聖なるものであれば、枝もそうです。
ja.B: 初穂として献げられたパン生地が聖なるものであれば、こね粉の全体も聖なるものです。根が聖なるものであれば、枝もそうです。
ja.R: パン生地の最初のひとかたまりが神にささげられて聖なるものとなれば、こね粉の全部も聖なるものです。そして、木の根が聖なるものなら、その枝も聖なるものです。

decisions.choice: the offering of the first of the dough, Numbers 15:17-21
decisions.reason: Israel was to offer to God a cake from the first of its dough. Once that part was given, the whole batch could be used, as belonging to God.

decisions.choice: holy: set apart for God, belonging to him
decisions.reason: Holiness here is belonging to God, not moral goodness.

decisions.choice: the firstfruits and the root: Israel's forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
alternatives: the first Jewish believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: Verse 28 says Israel is loved "because of the fathers", which suggests the root is the patriarchs, to whom the promises were made. Some take the firstfruits to be the Jewish believers (the remnant) and the root to be the patriarchs.

decisions.choice: the portion of dough offered as firstfruits (B); the first piece of dough is offered to God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the firstfruit is, since "lump" refers to dough.

decisions.choice: "첫 [반죽]" (L); "처음 바친 반죽" (B); "반죽의 첫 덩이를 하나님께 바치다" (R)
decisions.reason: The offering is the first of the dough (Numbers 15:17-21, meaning decision), so "첫 열매" (8:23) would suggest fruit. "떡" is avoided as everywhere (bread is "빵"); dough is "반죽".

decisions.choice: "phần đầu mùa" (L); "phần bột đầu tiên được dâng làm của đầu mùa" (B)
decisions.reason: The firstfruits here are the first of the dough offered to God (m1, Numbers 15). "Trái đầu mùa" (8:23) would mean fruit, so Literal says "phần đầu mùa" and Balanced says what was offered.
The Greek noun is singular, but Portuguese uses this word in the plural; Literal follows usage, and the meaning (one offering of dough) is unchanged.
በኩራት is the Bible word for the first portion offered to God (Numbers 15:17-21); Balanced adds that it is a portion of dough, and Readable explains it.

The picture is the offering of the first of the dough (m1). "初穂" is the familiar word for the first part given to God; since it suggests grain, Balanced names the dough, and Readable drops the church word and describes the offering.

source.text: Εἰ δέ τινες τῶν κλάδων ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ ἀγριέλαιος ὢν ἐνεκεντρίσθης ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ συγκοινωνὸς τῆς ῥίζης τῆς πιότητος τῆς ἐλαίας ἐγένου, μὴ κατακαυχῶ τῶν κλάδων· εἰ δὲ κατακαυχᾶσαι, οὐ σὺ τὴν ῥίζαν βαστάζεις ἀλλὰ ἡ ῥίζα σέ.

records.literal_gloss: If but some of the branches were broken off, and you a wild olive being were grafted in among them and fellow-sharer of the root of the richness of the olive tree became, \v 18 not boast over the branches; if but you boast, not you the root support but the root you.

en.L: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became a sharer of the root of the richness of the olive tree, \v 18 do not boast over the branches; but if you do boast, [remember that] it is not you [who] support the root, but the root [supports] you.
en.B: Now if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and now share in the rich root of the olive tree, \v 18 do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, remember: you do not hold up the root; the root holds you up.
en.R: Some of the branches of the olive tree were broken off. You are like a shoot from a wild olive tree that was joined onto the tree among the other branches. Now you share the rich sap that comes up from its root. \v 18 So do not think you are better than the natural branches. If you are tempted to boast, remember this: You do not hold up the root. The root holds you up.

es.L: Pero si algunas de las ramas fueron desgajadas, y tú, siendo olivo silvestre, fuiste injertado entre ellas y llegaste a ser copartícipe de la raíz de la riqueza del olivo, \v 18 no te jactes contra las ramas; pero si te jactas, [recuerda que] no sostienes tú a la raíz, sino la raíz a ti.
es.B: Ahora bien, si algunas de las ramas fueron arrancadas y tú, aunque eras un brote de olivo silvestre, fuiste injertado entre ellas y ahora participas de la rica raíz del olivo, \v 18 no te jactes frente a las ramas. Y si te jactas, recuerda: no cargas tú con la raíz; la raíz carga contigo.
es.R: Algunas ramas del olivo fueron arrancadas. Tú eres como un brote de olivo silvestre que fue injertado, es decir, unido al árbol entre las otras ramas. Ahora recibes la savia abundante que sube de su raíz. \v 18 Así que no mires con desprecio a las ramas naturales. Si sientes la tentación de jactarte, recuerda esto: Tú no sostienes la raíz. La raíz te sostiene a ti.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa baadhi ya matawi yalivunjwa, nawe, ukiwa mzeituni mwitu, ulipandikizwa kati yao na ukawa mshiriki wa mzizi wa unono wa mzeituni, \v 18 usijigambe juu ya matawi; na ikiwa unajigamba, [jua kwamba] wewe hautegemezi mzizi, bali mzizi unakutegemeza wewe.
sw.B: Basi, ikiwa baadhi ya matawi yalivunjwa, nawe, ingawa ulikuwa chipukizi la mzeituni mwitu, ukapandikizwa katikati yao na sasa unashiriki mzizi wenye rutuba wa mzeituni, \v 18 usijigambe mbele ya matawi. Ukijigamba, kumbuka: wewe hauushikilii mzizi; mzizi ndio unaokushikilia wewe.
sw.R: Baadhi ya matawi ya mzeituni yalivunjwa. Wewe ni kama chipukizi la mzeituni mwitu lililopandikizwa, yaani, kuunganishwa na mti huo kati ya matawi mengine. Sasa unapata utomvu mwingi unaopanda kutoka kwenye mzizi wake. \v 18 Kwa hiyo usiyadharau matawi ya asili. Ukishawishika kujigamba, kumbuka hili: Wewe hauushikilii mzizi. Mzizi ndio unaokushikilia wewe.

fr.L: Mais si quelques-unes des branches ont été cassées, et que toi, étant un olivier sauvage, tu as été greffé parmi elles et que tu es devenu participant de la racine de la richesse de l’olivier, \v 18 ne te glorifie pas aux dépens des branches ; mais si tu te glorifies, [sache que] ce n’est pas toi [qui] portes la racine, mais la racine [qui te porte], toi.
fr.B: Or si quelques branches ont été cassées, et si toi, qui n’étais qu’une pousse d’olivier sauvage, tu as été greffé parmi elles et tu as maintenant part à la riche racine de l’olivier, \v 18 ne te glorifie pas aux dépens des branches. Si tu te glorifies, rappelle-toi : ce n’est pas toi qui portes la racine, c’est la racine qui te porte.
fr.R: Certaines branches de l’olivier ont été cassées. Toi, tu es comme une pousse d’olivier sauvage qui a été greffée sur l’arbre, parmi les autres branches. Maintenant, tu profites de la riche sève qui monte de la racine. \v 18 Alors, ne pense pas que tu vaux mieux que les branches naturelles. Si tu as envie de te vanter, souviens-toi de ceci : ce n’est pas toi qui portes la racine. C’est la racine qui te porte.

ko.L: 그런데 가지들 가운데 얼마가 꺾이고, 야생 올리브 나무인 당신이 그들 사이에 접붙여져서 올리브 나무의 기름진 뿌리에 함께 참여하는 사람이 되었다면, \v 18 그 가지들을 향하여 자랑하지 마십시오. 자랑한다면, [기억하십시오.] 당신이 뿌리를 지탱하는 것이 아니라 뿌리가 당신을 [지탱합니다].
ko.B: 가지들 가운데 얼마가 꺾여 나가고, 야생 올리브 나무의 가지인 당신이 그 가지들 사이에 접붙여져서 이제 올리브 나무의 기름진 뿌리에서 나오는 양분을 함께 받고 있다면, \v 18 그 가지들을 깔보며 자랑하지 마십시오. 자랑하고 싶다면 기억하십시오. 당신이 뿌리를 지탱하는 것이 아니라, 뿌리가 당신을 지탱합니다.
ko.R: 올리브 나무의 가지들 가운데 몇 개가 꺾여 나갔습니다. 당신은 야생 올리브 나무에서 잘라 온 가지와 같습니다. 그 가지가 다른 가지들 사이에 접붙여진 것입니다. 이제 당신은 그 나무의 뿌리에서 올라오는 풍성한 진액을 함께 받고 있습니다. \v 18 그러니 원래 가지들보다 당신이 더 낫다고 생각하지 마십시오. 자랑하고 싶은 마음이 들면 이것을 기억하십시오. 당신이 뿌리를 떠받치는 것이 아닙니다. 뿌리가 당신을 떠받치고 있습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu một vài nhánh đã bị bẻ đi, còn bạn, vốn là cây ô-liu dại, đã được tháp vào giữa chúng và trở nên người cùng dự phần vào rễ [đầy] nhựa béo của cây ô-liu, \v 18 thì đừng khoe mình hơn các nhánh; còn nếu bạn khoe mình, [hãy nhớ rằng] không phải bạn nâng đỡ rễ, mà là rễ [nâng đỡ] bạn.
vi.B: Nếu có mấy nhánh đã bị bẻ đi, còn bạn, vốn là chồi ô-liu dại, lại được tháp vào giữa các nhánh ấy và nay cùng hưởng rễ đầy nhựa sống của cây ô-liu, \v 18 thì đừng khoe khoang hơn các nhánh ấy. Nếu bạn muốn khoe khoang, hãy nhớ rằng: không phải bạn nâng đỡ rễ, nhưng rễ nâng đỡ bạn.
vi.R: Một số nhánh của cây ô-liu đã bị bẻ đi. Bạn giống như một chồi non từ cây ô-liu dại được ghép vào cây ấy, giữa những nhánh khác. Bây giờ bạn được hưởng nhựa sống dồi dào từ rễ cây. \v 18 Vậy đừng nghĩ mình hơn những nhánh vốn có của cây. Nếu bạn bị cám dỗ để khoe khoang, hãy nhớ điều này: Không phải bạn nâng đỡ rễ. Chính rễ nâng đỡ bạn.

pt.L: Mas, se alguns dos ramos foram quebrados, e você, sendo oliveira brava, foi enxertado entre eles e se tornou participante da raiz da seiva da oliveira, \v 18 não se glorie contra os ramos; mas, se você se gloria, [lembre-se de que] não é você [que] sustenta a raiz, mas a raiz [sustenta] você.
pt.B: Ora, se alguns dos ramos foram quebrados, e você, mesmo sendo um broto de oliveira brava, foi enxertado entre eles e agora participa da rica raiz da oliveira, \v 18 não se orgulhe à custa dos ramos. Se você se orgulhar, lembre-se: não é você que sustenta a raiz; é a raiz que sustenta você.
pt.R: Alguns galhos da oliveira foram quebrados. Você é como um broto de uma oliveira do mato que foi enxertado na árvore, no meio dos outros galhos. Agora você recebe a seiva rica que sobe da raiz. \v 18 Por isso, não se ache melhor do que os galhos naturais. Se você tiver vontade de se orgulhar, lembre-se disto: não é você que sustenta a raiz. É a raiz que sustenta você.

am.L: ነገር ግን ከቅርንጫፎቹ አንዳንዶቹ ተሰብረው ከሆነ፣ አንተም የዱር ወይራ ሆነህ ሳለህ በመካከላቸው ተከትበህ የወይራውን ዛፍ የሥሩን ልምላሜ ተካፋይ ከሆንክ፣ \v 18 በቅርንጫፎቹ ላይ አትመካ፤ ብትመካ ግን [አስታውስ፤] ሥሩን የምትሸከመው አንተ አይደለህም፤ ሥሩ አንተን [ይሸከምሃል] እንጂ።
am.B: ከቅርንጫፎቹ አንዳንዶቹ ተሰብረው፣ አንተም የዱር ወይራ ቅርንጫፍ ሆነህ ሳለ በመካከላቸው ተከትበህ፣ አሁን የወይራውን ዛፍ የበለጸገ ሥር የምትካፈል ከሆንክ፣ \v 18 በቅርንጫፎቹ ላይ አትመካ። ብትመካ ግን ይህን አስታውስ፤ ሥሩን የምትደግፈው አንተ አይደለህም፤ ሥሩ ነው አንተን የሚደግፍህ።
am.R: ከወይራው ዛፍ ቅርንጫፎች አንዳንዶቹ ተሰብረዋል። አንተ ደግሞ ከዱር ወይራ ዛፍ እንደ ተወሰደ ቀንበጥ ነህ፤ በሌሎቹ ቅርንጫፎች መካከል በዛፉ ላይ ተቀጥለሃል። አሁን ከሥሩ የሚወጣውን ሕይወት ሰጪ ጭማቂ ትካፈላለህ። \v 18 ስለዚህ ከተፈጥሮ ቅርንጫፎቹ እንደምትበልጥ አታስብ። ለመመካት ብትፈተን ይህን አስታውስ፤ ሥሩን ደግፈህ የያዝከው አንተ አይደለህም። ሥሩ ነው አንተን ደግፎ የያዘህ።

ru.L: Если же некоторые из ветвей были отломлены, а ты, будучи дикой маслиной, был привит среди них и стал соучастником корня и сока маслины, \v 18 не превозносись над ветвями; если же превозносишься, [помни, что] не ты держишь корень, но корень тебя.
ru.B: Если же некоторые ветви были отломлены, а ты, побег дикой маслины, был привит среди них и теперь питаешься от сочного корня маслины, \v 18 не превозносись над ветвями. А если превозносишься, помни: не ты держишь корень, а корень держит тебя.
ru.R: Некоторые ветви оливкового дерева были отломлены. Ты похож на побег дикой оливы, который привили к дереву среди других ветвей. Теперь ты получаешь живительный сок, который поднимается от его корня. \v 18 Поэтому не думай, что ты лучше родных ветвей. Если тебе хочется хвалиться, помни: не ты держишь корень. Корень держит тебя.

hi.L: पर यदि कुछ डालियाँ तोड़ी गईं, और तुम जंगली जैतून होकर उनके बीच में कलम किए गए और जैतून की चिकनाई की जड़ के सहभागी बने, \v 18 तो डालियों पर घमंड न करना; और यदि तुम घमंड करो, [तो जान लो कि] तुम जड़ को नहीं सँभालते, पर जड़ तुम्हें।
hi.B: अब यदि कुछ डालियाँ तोड़ दी गईं, और तुम, जो जंगली जैतून की टहनी थे, उनके बीच कलम किए गए और अब जैतून की उपजाऊ जड़ में भागी हो, \v 18 तो उन डालियों पर घमंड मत करो। यदि तुम घमंड करो, तो याद रखो: तुम जड़ को नहीं सँभालते; जड़ तुम्हें सँभालती है।
hi.R: जैतून के पेड़ की कुछ डालियाँ तोड़ दी गईं। तुम जंगली जैतून की उस टहनी जैसे हो जिसे दूसरी डालियों के बीच उस पेड़ में जोड़ दिया गया। अब तुम उस भरपूर रस में भागी हो जो उसकी जड़ से ऊपर आता है। \v 18 इसलिए यह मत सोचो कि तुम उन असली डालियों से बेहतर हो। अगर तुम्हें घमंड करने का मन हो, तो यह याद रखो: तुम जड़ को नहीं सँभालते। जड़ तुम्हें सँभालती है।

uk.L: А якщо деякі з гілок були відламані, а ти, бувши дикою маслиною, був прищеплений між ними і став спільником кореня, [що дає] поживний сік маслини, \v 18 не хвалися перед гілками; а якщо хвалишся, [памʼятай, що] не ти тримаєш корінь, а корінь тебе.
uk.B: Якщо ж деякі гілки були відламані, а ти, хоч і пагін дикої маслини, був прищеплений між ними і тепер маєш частку в багатому корені маслини, \v 18 не хвалися перед гілками. А якщо хвалишся, памʼятай: не ти тримаєш корінь, а корінь тримає тебе.
uk.R: Деякі гілки маслини були відламані. Ти — наче пагін з дикої маслини, який прищепили до дерева серед інших гілок. Тепер ти живишся поживним соком, що йде від її кореня. \v 18 Тож не думай, що ти кращий за природні гілки. Якщо тобі хочеться хвалитися, памʼятай: не ти тримаєш корінь. Корінь тримає тебе.

ja.L: しかし、もし枝のいくつかが折り取られ、野生のオリーブであるあなたがその間に接ぎ木されて、オリーブの木の根の豊かさにともにあずかる者となったのなら、\v 18 その枝に対して誇ってはなりません。しかし、もし誇るなら、根を支えているのはあなたではなく、根があなたを[支えているのです]。
ja.B: さて、もし枝のいくつかが折り取られ、野生のオリーブの枝であるあなたが、その間に接ぎ木されて、オリーブの木の豊かな根にともにあずかるようになったのなら、\v 18 その枝に対して誇ってはなりません。たとえ誇るとしても、覚えておきなさい。あなたが根を支えているのではなく、根があなたを支えているのです。
ja.R: オリーブの木の枝のいくつかは、折り取られました。あなたは、野生のオリーブの木から取った枝のようなもので、ほかの枝の間に接ぎ木されたのです。今あなたは、根から上がってくる豊かな養分を分けてもらっています。\v 18 ですから、もとからある枝よりも自分のほうが上だと思わないでください。誇りたくなったら、このことを覚えていてください。あなたが根を支えているのではありません。根があなたを支えているのです。

decisions.reason: The prophets called Israel an olive tree planted by God (Jeremiah 11:16, Hosea 14:6). The broken branches are unbelieving Israelites; the wild shoot is the Gentile believer.

decisions.choice: you: one Gentile believer, addressed as an example
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to an imagined Gentile listener in the singular, as he does in 2:1-5 and 9:19-20, to warn all the Gentile believers.

decisions.choice: grafting a wild shoot into a cultivated tree
decisions.reason: Farmers grafted cultivated shoots onto wild stock, not the reverse; Paul himself says the grafting he describes is "contrary to nature" (verse 24). The unusual picture shows that the Gentiles' place is God's gift.

decisions.choice: "the root of the richness": the rich root
alternatives: "the root and the richness of the olive tree"
"the richness of the olive tree", without "the root"
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts have two genitives in a row, "of the root of the richness"; some manuscripts add "and" between them, and others leave out "the root". The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check the details against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: richness: the rich sap that nourishes the tree
decisions.reason: The word means fatness; the olive tree's richness is the life it draws from its root and gives to its branches.

decisions.choice: You are like a shoot from a wild olive tree that was joined onto the tree among the other branches
alternatives: you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison explicit and explains grafting.

decisions.choice: do not think you are better than the natural branches
alternatives: do not boast over the branches
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of boasting over others: looking down on them. The branches are those that belong to the tree by nature (verse 21).
Here Paul speaks to one imagined Gentile listener in the singular (m2), so Spanish uses "tú" and its verb forms, which are the same in Latin America and Spain and need no setting.

"Acebuche" is the exact word for the wild olive, familiar from older Spanish Bibles, but many readers do not know it. "Olivo silvestre" says the same plainly and keeps the contrast with the olive tree at every level.

"Mzeituni mwitu" is the wild olive and "kupandikiza" the ordinary word for grafting. Readable adds "yaani, kuunganishwa na mti huo" (that is, joined to the tree) to explain grafting, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "당신" with 합쇼체 for the singular "you" in verses 17-24, as at 2:1 and 8:2
decisions.reason: Paul addresses one Gentile believer as an example (meaning decision); the letter's 합쇼체 is kept with "당신" for the singular, as for the imagined listener in chapters 2 and 9.

decisions.choice: "올리브 나무", "야생 올리브 나무", "접붙이다" at every level, through verse 24
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide prefers the modern "올리브" ("올리브 산") to the older church word "감람".
The Greek leaves the thought unspoken: "if you boast, [know that] not you support the root"; Korean needs the verb.
Paul addresses one Gentile believer as an example (m2). As in 2:1 and 8:2, the singular reader is "bạn"; "anh chị em" would turn it back into the plural of 11:13.
"Tháp" is the gardener's word for grafting a shoot onto another tree (m3); Readable uses the more common "ghép". "Chiết" is layering a branch to root it, a different technique.

Literal keeps "khoe mình", the word for this family through the letter (2:17). Here it is boasting over others ("over the branches"), so Balanced and Readable say "khoe khoang", as in 3:27, not the "tự hào" of 2:17.

Paul speaks to one imagined Gentile believer (meaning decision m2), so Portuguese uses the singular "você" between people, as it does for the rest of the olive tree passage (verses 17-24); "tu" is kept for God.

decisions.choice: oliveira brava (L, B); oliveira do mato (R)
decisions.reason: "Oliveira brava" is the plain Brazilian name for a wild olive; "zambujeiro" is the botanical and European word few Brazilian readers know. Readable says "do mato", the everyday word for wild plants.

decisions.choice: መከተብ (to graft, L, B); መቀጠል (to join on, R)
decisions.reason: ከተበ is the word for grafting a shoot into a tree; Readable says ተቀጥለሃል, 'you were joined on', as the English Readable does. The same verbs continue to 11:24.
Paul turns to one Gentile believer as an example (meaning note m2), so the address is singular here to 11:24, as the Greek is.
"Маслина" is the traditional Bible word for the olive tree; Readable uses the everyday "олива".
Paul turns to one Gentile believer as an example (meaning decision m2), with the Greek singular, so Russian says "ты" here, though he says "вы" to the readers elsewhere.

Paul addresses one Gentile believer as an example (meaning decision m2) with the same तुम he uses for all his readers; the singular is clear from the picture of one branch. The same holds through verse 24.
"कलम करना" is the gardener's word for grafting; Readable says what grafting does.
Paul addresses one Gentile believer as an example (m2), with the Greek singular, so Ukrainian keeps "ти"; the tree is "маслина", the wild one "дика маслина", and grafting "прищепити" throughout.

decisions.choice: singular "あなた" (not "あなたがた" or "みなさん") through verses 17-24
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to one imagined Gentile believer as an example (m2), so every level keeps the singular "あなた" for this passage, as it does for the readers' plural elsewhere with "あなたがた" and "みなさん".

decisions.choice: "接ぎ木される"; "野生のオリーブ"
decisions.reason: "接ぎ木" is the ordinary Japanese word for grafting and is used for the whole olive-tree picture through verse 24.

source.text: ἐρεῖς οὖν· Ἐξεκλάσθησαν κλάδοι ἵνα ἐγὼ ἐγκεντρισθῶ.

records.literal_gloss: You will say then: Were broken off branches that I might be grafted in.

en.L: You will say then, "Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in."
en.B: Then you will say, "Branches were broken off to let me be grafted in."
en.R: Then you might say, "God broke those branches off to make room for me."

es.L: Dirás entonces: «Fueron desgajadas ramas para que yo fuera injertado.»
es.B: Entonces dirás: «Se desgajaron ramas para que yo pudiera ser injertado.»
es.R: Entonces tal vez digas: «Dios arrancó esas ramas para hacerme lugar a mí.»

sw.L: Basi utasema: "Matawi yalivunjwa ili mimi nipandikizwe."
sw.B: Hapo utasema: "Matawi yalivunjwa ili nipate kupandikizwa mimi."
sw.R: Labda utasema: "Mungu aliyavunja matawi hayo ili anipatie nafasi."

fr.L: Tu diras donc : « Des branches ont été cassées pour que moi, je sois greffé. »
fr.B: Tu diras alors : « Des branches ont été cassées pour que moi, je puisse être greffé. »
fr.R: Tu pourrais alors dire : « Dieu a cassé ces branches pour me faire de la place. »

ko.L: 그러면 당신은 말할 것입니다. "가지들이 꺾인 것은 내가 접붙여지게 하려는 것이었습니다."
ko.B: 그러면 당신은 "가지들이 꺾여 나간 것은 내가 접붙여지게 하려는 것이었습니다" 하고 말할 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러면 당신은 이렇게 말할지도 모릅니다. "하나님께서 그 가지들을 꺾으신 것은 내가 들어갈 자리를 만드시려는 것이었습니다."

vi.L: Vậy bạn sẽ nói: "Các nhánh đã bị bẻ đi để tôi được tháp vào."
vi.B: Bấy giờ bạn sẽ nói: "Những nhánh kia đã bị bẻ đi để tôi được tháp vào."
vi.R: Rồi có thể bạn sẽ nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã bẻ những nhánh ấy đi để có chỗ cho tôi."

pt.L: Você dirá, então: "Ramos foram quebrados para que eu fosse enxertado."
pt.B: Então você vai dizer: "Ramos foram quebrados para que eu fosse enxertado."
pt.R: Então você pode dizer: "Deus quebrou aqueles galhos para abrir espaço para mim."

am.L: እንግዲህ፦ «እኔ እንድከተብ ቅርንጫፎች ተሰበሩ» ትላለህ።
am.B: ከዚያም፦ «እኔ እንድከተብ ቅርንጫፎች ተሰበሩ» ትላለህ።
am.R: ከዚያም፦ «እግዚአብሔር እነዚያን ቅርንጫፎች የሰበራቸው ለእኔ ቦታ ለማዘጋጀት ነው» ትል ይሆናል።

ru.L: Ты скажешь тогда: «Ветви отломлены, чтобы мне быть привитым.»
ru.B: Тогда ты скажешь: «Ветви отломили, чтобы привить меня.»
ru.R: Тогда ты можешь сказать: «Бог отломил эти ветви, чтобы освободить место для меня.»

hi.L: फिर तुम कहोगे, "डालियाँ इसलिए तोड़ी गईं कि मैं कलम किया जाऊँ।"
hi.B: तब तुम कहोगे, "डालियाँ इसलिए तोड़ी गईं कि मैं कलम किया जा सकूँ।"
hi.R: तब शायद तुम कहो, "परमेश्वर ने वे डालियाँ इसलिए तोड़ीं कि मेरे लिए जगह बने।"

uk.L: Отже, скажеш: «Гілки були відламані, щоб я був прищеплений.»
uk.B: Тоді ти скажеш: «Гілки відламали, щоб прищепити мене.»
uk.R: Тоді ти можеш сказати: «Бог відламав ті гілки, щоб звільнити місце для мене.»

ja.L: それで、あなたは言うでしょう。「枝が折り取られたのは、わたしが接ぎ木されるためだった」と。
ja.B: すると、あなたは言うでしょう。「枝が折り取られたのは、わたしが接ぎ木されるためだったのだ」と。
ja.R: するとあなたは、「神があの枝を折り取られたのは、わたしの場所を空けるためだったのだ」と言うかもしれません。

decisions.choice: so that: the Gentile's claim that God's purpose was to make room for him
decisions.reason: The imagined speaker takes the breaking off as having been done for his sake. Paul grants the fact in verse 20 but not the pride behind it.

decisions.choice: God broke those branches off to make room for me
alternatives: branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who broke the branches off, as verse 21 implies, and says what grafting in means for the speaker.

decisions.choice: the imagined speaker's words in 합쇼체 ("... 것이었습니다"), as the objector's words at 3:1 and 9:19
decisions.reason: The imagined objector speaks to Paul in 합쇼체 through the letter.

source.text: καλῶς· τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἐξεκλάσθησαν, σὺ δὲ τῇ πίστει ἕστηκας.

records.literal_gloss: Well; by the unbelief they were broken off, but you by the faith stand.

en.L: Well [said]; they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith.
en.B: That is true. They were broken off because of their unbelief, but you stand firm by faith.
en.R: That is true. But they were broken off because they did not believe. And you are still there only because of your faith.

es.L: Bien [dicho]; por la incredulidad fueron desgajadas, y tú por la fe te mantienes en pie.
es.B: Es cierto. Fueron desgajadas por su incredulidad, pero tú te mantienes firme por la fe.
es.R: Es verdad. Pero esas ramas fueron arrancadas porque no creyeron. Y tú sigues allí solo por tu fe.

sw.L: Vema; kwa sababu ya kutoamini yalivunjwa, lakini wewe kwa imani umesimama.
sw.B: Ni kweli. Yalivunjwa kwa sababu ya kutoamini kwao, lakini wewe umesimama imara kwa imani.
sw.R: Ni kweli. Lakini matawi hayo yalivunjwa kwa sababu ya kutoamini kwao. Nawe bado uko pale kwa sababu ya imani yako tu.

fr.L: Bien ; c’est à cause de l’incrédulité qu’elles ont été cassées, mais toi, tu tiens debout par la foi.
fr.B: C’est vrai. Elles ont été cassées à cause de leur incrédulité, mais toi, tu tiens ferme par la foi.
fr.R: C’est vrai. Mais ces branches ont été cassées parce qu’elles ne croyaient pas. Et toi, tu n’es encore là que grâce à ta foi.

ko.L: 옳습니다. 그들은 믿지 않음으로 꺾였고, 당신은 믿음으로 서 있습니다.
ko.B: 맞습니다. 그들은 믿지 않았기 때문에 꺾여 나갔고, 당신은 믿음으로 굳게 서 있습니다.
ko.R: 그 말은 맞습니다. 그러나 그들이 꺾여 나간 것은 믿지 않았기 때문입니다. 그리고 당신이 아직 그 나무에 붙어 있는 것은 오직 믿음 때문입니다.

vi.L: Đúng vậy; họ đã bị bẻ đi vì sự không tin, còn bạn đứng vững bởi đức tin.
vi.B: Điều đó đúng. Họ đã bị bẻ đi vì không tin, còn bạn đứng vững nhờ đức tin.
vi.R: Điều đó đúng. Nhưng họ bị bẻ đi vì họ không tin. Còn bạn vẫn ở đó chỉ nhờ đức tin của bạn.

pt.L: Bem [dito]; foram quebrados pela incredulidade, mas você está de pé pela fé.
pt.B: É verdade. Eles foram quebrados por causa da incredulidade, mas você se mantém firme pela fé.
pt.R: É verdade. Mas eles foram quebrados porque não creram. E você só continua ali por causa da sua fé.

am.L: መልካም [ተናገርህ]፤ ባለማመናቸው ተሰበሩ፤ አንተ ግን በእምነት ቆመሃል።
am.B: ይህ እውነት ነው። ባለማመናቸው ምክንያት ተሰበሩ፤ አንተ ግን በእምነት ጸንተህ ቆመሃል።
am.R: ይህ እውነት ነው። ነገር ግን የተሰበሩት ስላላመኑ ነው። አንተም አሁንም በዛፉ ላይ ያለኸው በእምነትህ ብቻ ነው።

ru.L: Хорошо; они отломлены неверием, а ты стоишь верой.
ru.B: Это правда. Они были отломлены из-за своего неверия, а ты держишься верой.
ru.R: Это правда. Но они были отломлены, потому что не верили. А ты остаёшься на дереве только благодаря своей вере.

hi.L: ठीक; वे अविश्वास के कारण तोड़ी गईं, पर तुम विश्वास से खड़े हो।
hi.B: यह सच है। वे अपने अविश्वास के कारण तोड़ी गईं, पर तुम विश्वास से दृढ़ खड़े हो।
hi.R: यह सच है। पर वे इसलिए तोड़ी गईं कि उन्होंने विश्वास नहीं किया। और तुम केवल अपने विश्वास के कारण अब भी पेड़ पर बने हुए हो।

uk.L: Добре; через невірство вони були відламані, а ти стоїш вірою.
uk.B: Це правда. Вони були відламані через своє невірство, а ти тримаєшся завдяки вірі.
uk.R: Це правда. Але їх відламали, бо вони не вірили. А ти все ще на дереві тільки завдяки своїй вірі.

ja.L: そのとおりです。彼らは不信仰によって折り取られ、あなたは信仰によって立っています。
ja.B: そのとおりです。彼らは不信仰のために折り取られましたが、あなたは信仰によってしっかり立っているのです。
ja.R: 確かにそうです。でも、彼らが折り取られたのは、信じなかったからです。そしてあなたが今もそこにいるのは、ただあなたの信仰によるのです。

decisions.choice: Well said: granted, that is true as far as it goes
decisions.reason: Paul agrees with the fact but goes on to correct the conclusion the speaker draws from it.
Set against "faith" in the same sentence, this is the unbelief of 10:16-21: refusing to believe the gospel.
The two datives give the cause on each side: unbelief led to the branches being broken off, and faith is how the Gentile stands.
Standing means keeping one's place on the tree; Readable continues the picture.
Readable brings out the contrast with the broken branches: faith, not anything else, keeps the Gentile on the tree.

decisions.choice: "믿지 않음" (L); "믿지 않았기 때문에" (B, R) for unbelief, here and in verse 23
decisions.reason: Unbelief is simply not believing (meaning decision); Korean keeps it tied to "믿음" and "믿다".
The word here is not believing (m2), set against faith. "Bất tín" was used in 3:3 for unfaithfulness, the other sense of the same Greek word, so the plain "không tin" is used here.
Unbelief here is refusing to believe the gospel, set against faith (m2). "不信仰" pairs with "信仰" in the same sentence; Readable uses the verb 信じる, kept at every level.

source.text: μὴ ὑψηλὰ φρόνει, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Not high things be minded, but fear;

en.L: Do not think lofty [thoughts], but fear.
en.B: Do not be proud, but fear.
en.R: So do not be proud. Fear God instead.

es.L: No pienses cosas altivas, sino teme.
es.B: No seas orgulloso, sino teme.
es.R: Así que no seas orgulloso. Más bien, teme a Dios.

sw.L: Usiwaze mambo ya juu, bali uogope.
sw.B: Usiwe na kiburi, bali uwe na hofu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo usijivune. Badala yake mche Mungu.

fr.L: N’aie pas de pensées hautaines, mais crains.
fr.B: Ne t’enorgueillis pas, mais crains.
fr.R: Alors, ne sois pas orgueilleux. Crains plutôt Dieu.

ko.L: 높은 [생각을] 품지 말고 두려워하십시오.
ko.B: 교만하지 말고 두려워하십시오.
ko.R: 그러니 교만하지 마십시오. 오히려 하나님을 두려워하십시오.

vi.L: Đừng nghĩ những [điều] cao ngạo, nhưng hãy kính sợ.
vi.B: Đừng kiêu ngạo, nhưng hãy kính sợ.
vi.R: Vậy đừng kiêu ngạo. Thay vào đó, hãy kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: Não pense coisas altivas, mas tema.
pt.B: Não seja orgulhoso, mas tema.
pt.R: Por isso, não seja orgulhoso. Em vez disso, tema a Deus.

am.L: ከፍ ያለ [ሐሳብ] አታስብ፤ ነገር ግን ፍራ።
am.B: አትታበይ፤ ነገር ግን ፍራ።
am.R: ስለዚህ አትኩራ። ይልቁንም እግዚአብሔርን ፍራ።

ru.L: Не мудрствуй высоко, но бойся.
ru.B: Не гордись, а бойся.
ru.R: Поэтому не гордись. Лучше бойся Бога.

hi.L: ऊँची बातें मत सोचो, पर डरो;
hi.B: घमंड मत करो, पर डरो।
hi.R: इसलिए घमंड मत करो। इसके बजाय परमेश्वर का भय मानो।

uk.L: Не думай високо [про себе], а бійся.
uk.B: Не будь гордим, а бійся.
uk.R: Тож не гордися. Краще бійся Бога.

ja.L: 高ぶったことを思ってはなりません。むしろ、恐れなさい。
ja.B: 思い上がってはなりません。むしろ恐れなさい。
ja.R: ですから、思い上がらないでください。むしろ、神を恐れてください。

decisions.choice: do not think high thoughts: do not be proud
decisions.reason: To "think high things" means to be arrogant, as in 12:16.

decisions.choice: fear: a reverent fear of God and his judgment
decisions.reason: The next verse gives the reason: God did not spare the natural branches. This is the fear that keeps a person humble before God, not general anxiety.
Readable names God as the one to be feared, as verse 21 makes clear.
The fear meant is reverent fear of God and his judgment (m2). "Kính sợ" is that reverence; "sợ" alone is only being afraid. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τῶν κατὰ φύσιν κλάδων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, οὐδὲ σοῦ φείσεται.

records.literal_gloss: If for the God the according to nature branches not spared, neither you will he spare.

en.L: For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spare you.
en.B: For if God did not spare the branches that grew naturally on the tree, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not spare you either.
en.R: God did not spare the branches that belonged to the tree by nature. So if you become proud, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not spare you either.

es.L: Porque si Dios no escatimó a las ramas naturales, tampoco te escatimará a ti.
es.B: Porque si Dios no escatimó a las ramas que crecían naturalmente en el árbol, tampoco te escatimará a ti.
es.R: Dios no libró de ser cortadas a las ramas que pertenecían al árbol por naturaleza. Así que, si te vuelves orgulloso, tampoco a ti te librará.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa Mungu hakuyahurumia matawi ya asili, wala wewe hatakuhurumia.
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa Mungu hakuyahurumia matawi yaliyoota kwa asili kwenye mti, hatakuhurumia wewe pia.
sw.R: Mungu hakuyahurumia matawi yaliyokuwa ya mti huo kwa asili. Kwa hiyo ukijivuna, hatakuhurumia wewe pia.

fr.L: Car si Dieu n’a pas épargné les branches naturelles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’épargnera pas non plus.
fr.B: Car si Dieu n’a pas épargné les branches qui avaient poussé naturellement sur l’arbre, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’épargnera pas non plus.
fr.R: Dieu n’a pas épargné les branches qui appartenaient à l’arbre par nature. Alors, si tu deviens orgueilleux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’épargnera pas non plus.

ko.L: 하나님께서 본성을 따라 [난] 가지들을 아끼지 않으셨다면, 당신도 아끼지 않으실 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 나무에 본래 붙어 있던 가지들도 아끼지 않으셨다면, 당신도 아끼지 않으실 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 원래 그 나무에 붙어 있던 가지들도 아끼지 않으셨습니다. 그러니 당신이 교만해지면, 하나님께서는 당신도 아끼지 않으실 것입니다.

vi.L: Vì nếu Đức Chúa Trời đã không tha các nhánh tự nhiên, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng sẽ không tha bạn.
vi.B: Vì nếu Đức Chúa Trời đã không tha những nhánh vốn mọc tự nhiên trên cây, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng sẽ không tha bạn.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã không tha những nhánh vốn thuộc về cây từ đầu. Vậy nếu bạn trở nên kiêu ngạo, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng sẽ không tha bạn.

pt.L: Pois, se Deus não poupou os ramos naturais, também não poupará você.
pt.B: Pois, se Deus não poupou os ramos que cresceram naturalmente na árvore, também não vai poupar você.
pt.R: Deus não poupou os galhos que eram da árvore por natureza. Então, se você ficar orgulhoso, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} também não vai poupar você.

am.L: እግዚአብሔር በተፈጥሮ ለሆኑት ቅርንጫፎች ካልራራላቸው፣ ለአንተም አይራራልህምና።
am.B: ምክንያቱም እግዚአብሔር በተፈጥሮ በዛፉ ላይ ላደጉት ቅርንጫፎች ካልራራላቸው ለአንተም አይራራልህም።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር በተፈጥሮ የዛፉ ለሆኑት ቅርንጫፎች አልራራላቸውም። ስለዚህ አንተ ብትኩራ ለአንተም አይራራልህም።

ru.L: Ведь если Бог не пощадил природных ветвей, то и тебя не пощадит.
ru.B: Ведь если Бог не пощадил ветвей, которые выросли на дереве естественно, то и тебя {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не пощадит.
ru.R: Бог не пощадил ветвей, которые принадлежали дереву от природы. Поэтому если ты станешь гордиться, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не пощадит и тебя.

hi.L: क्योंकि यदि परमेश्वर ने स्वाभाविक डालियों को न छोड़ा, तो तुम्हें भी न छोड़ेंगे।
hi.B: क्योंकि यदि परमेश्वर ने उन डालियों को नहीं छोड़ा जो पेड़ पर स्वाभाविक रूप से उगी थीं, तो वे तुम्हें भी नहीं छोड़ेंगे।
hi.R: परमेश्वर ने उन डालियों को नहीं छोड़ा जो स्वभाव से उस पेड़ की थीं। इसलिए अगर तुम घमंडी हो जाओ, तो वे तुम्हें भी नहीं छोड़ेंगे।

uk.L: Бо якщо Бог не пощадив природних гілок, то й тебе {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не пощадить.
uk.B: Бо якщо Бог не пощадив гілок, що природно росли на дереві, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не пощадить і тебе.
uk.R: Бог не пощадив гілок, які за природою належали дереву. Тож якщо ти загордишся, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не пощадить і тебе.

ja.L: なぜなら、もし神が本来の枝を惜しまれなかったとすれば、あなたをも惜しまれないからです。
ja.B: 神が、もともと木に生えていた枝さえ容赦されなかったのなら、あなたも容赦されないでしょう。
ja.R: 神は、もともとその木のものだった枝を容赦されませんでした。ですから、もしあなたが思い上がるなら、神はあなたも容赦されないでしょう。

decisions.choice: if God did not spare: since he did not spare
decisions.reason: The "if" states a fact Paul has already described: the natural branches were broken off.

decisions.choice: the natural branches: Israelites by birth
decisions.reason: Branches that grew on the tree "by nature" are Jews, members of Israel by descent, in contrast to the grafted wild shoot.

alternatives: some manuscripts add "perhaps": "perhaps he will not spare you either"
decisions.reason: A number of early manuscripts soften the warning with a word meaning "perhaps"; other early manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check the details against the SBLGNT apparatus.
Readable states the condition the warning assumes, from verse 20 ("do not be proud") and verse 22 ("if you continue in his kindness").

Older Spanish Bibles say "no perdonó", but "perdonar" is the word for forgiving sins, and here the verb means to spare from punishment. "Escatimar" has that sense (as in 8:32); Readable says plainly that God did not keep the branches from being cut off.
"Kuhurumia" (to have pity on, to spare) says that God did not hold back his judgment. "Kurehemu" is kept for the mercy of verses 30-32, a different Greek word.

Portuguese leaves out the subject pronoun where God has just been named, so Literal and Balanced have no deity_pronoun span where the English has "he"; Readable names the subject in a new sentence and keeps it.

decisions.choice: "惜しまれない" (L); "容赦されない" (B, R)
decisions.reason: To spare is to hold back from punishing. Literal keeps "惜しむ", the closest Japanese to the Greek verb; Balanced and Readable say "容赦する", which is clearer in a warning about judgment.

source.text: ἴδε οὖν χρηστότητα καὶ ἀποτομίαν θεοῦ· ἐπὶ μὲν τοὺς πεσόντας ἀποτομία, ἐπὶ δὲ σὲ χρηστότης θεοῦ, ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ἐκκοπήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: See then kindness and severity of God; upon on the one hand the having fallen severity, upon on the other hand you kindness of God, if you continue in the kindness, otherwise also you will be cut off.

en.L: See then [the] kindness and severity of God: on those who fell, severity, but on you, God's kindness, if you continue in [that] kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
en.B: Notice, then, both the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, as long as you continue in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off.
en.R: So think about how kind God is, and also how severe {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is. He was severe with those who fell. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is kind to you, as long as you keep living in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kindness. If you do not, you will be cut off too.

es.L: Mira, pues, [la] bondad y [la] severidad de Dios: sobre los que cayeron, severidad, pero sobre ti, bondad de Dios, si permaneces en [esa] bondad; de lo contrario, también tú serás cortado.
es.B: Fíjate, entonces, en la bondad y en la severidad de Dios: severidad hacia los que cayeron, pero bondad de Dios hacia ti, mientras sigas en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} bondad. De lo contrario, tú también serás cortado.
es.R: Así que piensa en lo bondadoso que es Dios, y también en lo severo que es. Fue severo con los que cayeron. Pero es bondadoso contigo, siempre que sigas viviendo en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} bondad. Si no, tú también serás cortado.

sw.L: Basi ona fadhili na ukali wa Mungu: juu ya wale walioanguka, ukali; lakini juu yako, fadhili za Mungu, ukidumu katika fadhili [hizo]; la sivyo, wewe pia utakatwa.
sw.B: Basi angalia fadhili na ukali wa Mungu: ukali kwa wale walioanguka, lakini fadhili za Mungu kwako, maadamu unadumu katika fadhili {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Vinginevyo, wewe pia utakatwa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo fikiri jinsi Mungu alivyo mwenye fadhili, na pia jinsi alivyo mkali. Aliwatendea kwa ukali wale walioanguka. Lakini anakutendea kwa fadhili, maadamu unaendelea kuishi katika fadhili {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Usipofanya hivyo, wewe pia utakatwa.

fr.L: Vois donc [la] bonté et [la] sévérité de Dieu : sur ceux qui sont tombés, [la] sévérité, mais sur toi, [la] bonté de Dieu, si tu demeures dans [cette] bonté ; autrement, toi aussi tu seras coupé.
fr.B: Considère donc la bonté et la sévérité de Dieu : sévérité envers ceux qui sont tombés, mais bonté de Dieu envers toi, pourvu que tu demeures dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonté. Sinon, toi aussi, tu seras coupé.
